instruction: Install Java JDK 17 (includes the JRE). Set JAVA_HOME to the JDK install directory (not a separate JRE folder) and add $JAVA_HOME/bin to your PATH. Install Visual Studio Code, then install the Java extension pack (Language Support for Java by Red Hat, Debugger for Java, Java Test Runner, Maven for Java). Restart VS Code and verify with `java -version` and `javac -version`.
Install the Flutter SDK and ensure `flutter` is on your PATH. Run `flutter doctor` and follow the prompts to install/fix any missing platform toolchains it reports.

Install Python 3.12 and the `uv` package manager. In your project directory, run `uv add` for the following packages: flask and flask-restful, then `uv sync`. Verify with `python3 --version` and `uv --version`.
Install GCC (C/C++) and build tools. Verify with `gcc --version`, `g++ --version`, `cmake --version`, and `make --version`, then build the project using the provided build instructions.
Install Clang (C/C++) and build tools. Verify with `clang --version`, `clang++ --version`, `cmake --version`, and `make --version`, then build the project using the provided build instructions.
Install Node.js (LTS) so you have `node` and `npm`. Verify with `node --version` and `npm --version`, then run `npm install` in the project directory.
Install Rust using rustup, then ensure `rustc` and `cargo` are available. Verify with `rustc --version` and `cargo --version`, then run `cargo build`.
Install Go and confirm the `go` command is available. Verify with `go version`, then run `go test ./...` in the project directory.
Install the .NET SDK (not just the runtime). Verify with `dotnet --info`, then run `dotnet restore` and `dotnet build`.
Install Ruby and Bundler. Verify with `ruby --version` and `bundle --version`, then run `bundle install`.
Install R (latest stable). Ensure the `R` executable is on your PATH, then verify with `R --version` and starting an interactive session with `R`.
Install RStudio Desktop and launch it once to confirm it detects your R installation. If it does not, configure RStudio to point to the installed R version in its settings.
Install MySQL Server, start the database service, and set a root password. Verify by connecting with `mysql -u root -p` and running `SELECT VERSION();`.
Install MySQL Workbench (GUI client). Create a new connection to your local MySQL server and test the connection using the credentials you set.
